Name: Trisha Boyles
Badge: Teacher as Researcher: Cultivating Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

I think actively reflecting on how our students engage with different strategies helps us to identify the most effective tools to bring/keep in our practices. I try to be a reflective practitioner, and it comes easily for the most part; however, it has been nice to be a little more intentional with these strategies. Moving forward, I realize that my younger students use the strategies better and more effectively. Perhaps this is because they are more apt to just do the things I ask them to do!

Share one artifact or anecdote from trying out your chosen strategy (e.g., a piece of student work, notes from your Writer’s Notebook, a classroom snapshot, or a brief story from the experience).:
What new questions or next steps are you leaving this module with? How might you continue to explore or build on this inquiry in your future teaching?:

All of my 7th graders did a solid job of creating good lists and free-writing during the sprints. I found that even some of the lower students did well with this as it gave them specific boundaries to work with and took away that pressure to figure out where to begin. I will continue to use the Quick Lists and Sprints next semester for everything from building research questions to ideas for general pieces of writing.
